entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sargis II Jaqeli was a Georgian prince (mtavari) and ruler of Principality of Samtskhe from 1308 to 1334. He played a crucial role in the politics of the region, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various Georgian and Mongol dynasties. Through his diplomatic efforts, Jaqeli secured a crucial trade agreement with the Mongols, ensuring the survival of his principality and cementing his legacy as a shrewd leader. This achievement had far-reaching consequences, as it helped to maintain stability in the region and facilitated the exchange of goods and ideas between East and West. The impact of Jaqeli's reign can still be seen in the modern-day borders of Georgia and the surrounding regions.

Jaqeli's rule was also marked by significant cultural developments, as he encouraged the patronage of artists and scholars. His court became a center of learning and creativity, attracting prominent intellectuals and writers from across the Islamic world. This cultural flowering had a lasting impact on the region, contributing to the rich tapestry of Georgian literature and art.

Despite his many achievements, Jaqeli's life was cut short when he died in 1334. His successor, however, continued his legacy, solidifying the principality's position as a major player in regional politics. The story of Sargis II Jaqeli serves as a testament to the enduring power of diplomacy and cultural exchange in shaping the course of history.

In the words of the 14th-century Georgian historian, 'Sargis II Jaqeli was a wise and just ruler, beloved by his people and respected by his peers.'
